title: Tiny Habits
author: BJ Fogg
blurb: BJ Fogg, a Stanford behavior scientist, argues that most attempts at change fail because of bad design, not weak character. His model says a behavior happens when motivation, ability, and a prompt come together at the same moment. Motivation rises and falls, so you shouldn't rely on it. Instead, make the new behavior so small it's almost effortless. Then attach it to something you already do every day, like flossing one tooth after brushing. Right after you do it, celebrate to create a feeling of success, because emotions are what wire habits in. Small habits then naturally grow and spread into bigger changes. The same principles, used in reverse, help you untangle unwanted habits. The result is a kind, practical, and repeatable method for lasting change.

lessons.t: It's Not You, It's the Design
lessons.b: Habits fail because of poor design rather than weak willpower, so you can stop blaming yourself and start redesigning.

lessons.t: Motivation, Ability, Prompt: The Behavior Formula
lessons.b: Any behavior happens only when motivation, ability, and a prompt all come together at the same moment.
Choose golden behaviors that you want to do, that make a real impact, and that you can actually do, rather than relying on fickle motivation.
Shrink a new habit until it's so easy you can do it even on your worst day, like flossing just one tooth.

lessons.b: Attach each tiny habit to something you already do with a simple recipe: after I do this, I will do that.
